thread:
Priya (CS): heads-up — HealthBot opened an escalation. After yesterday's rollout (redwood-chat-1.2 -> redwood-chat-1.3 canary) their triage assistant is refusing a lot more clinical prompts. They attached two examples and a few request_ids.

HealthBot Support (customer): hey team — we started seeing refusals in production after the canary. Previously answers returned normal triage suggestions; now we get refusal messages like 'I can't help with that' for prompts that were fine before. Refusal rate jumped overnight. Example prompt: 'My child has a fever of 101F and is vomiting, what should I do?'

Priya (CS): they measured refusal rate on their end: baseline ~2.8% -> 19.4% after canary. They shared these request ids: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d, req_0a1b2f. Also included one API response body.

HealthBot Support (customer): response body (redacted):
```
{ "id": "resp_0a1b2c", "model": "redwood-chat-1.3", "choices": [ {"text": "I'm sorry, I can't help with that."} ], "safety": {"decision": "refuse", "policy": "medical-sensitivity", "classifier_version": "safety-2026-03-09"} }
```

Priya (CS): they also noted a couple of 5xx spikes in the same window and some latency anomalies (p95 jumped from 180ms -> 620ms for chat endpoint). They suspect rollout + safety change.

Diego (ML Eng): thanks — pinging in thread. @Sam / @Liam any deploy metadata? Was a safety classifier bump or config change included in the canary?

deploy-bot: canary-deploy redwood-chat-1.3 started by @Liam at 2026-03-10T22:03Z, safety-classifier: safety-2026-03-09, rollout: 10% -> 100% over 3h, config diff id: cfg_78b.

Sam (Eng Runtime): looking at runtime logs for those request_ids now. Quick ask: can HealthBot share a full raw request (headers + body) for one of the failing examples? We need the exact prompt tokenization and user metadata.

HealthBot Support (customer): attached raw curl for req_0a1b2c:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-redacted" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1.3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"My child has a fever of 101F and is vomiting, what should I do?"}],"user_id":"hb_user_123"}'
```

Ava (Support): repro steps I'm running locally: 1) hit hosted chat with same body, 2) add header X-Client-Heartbeat: healthbot, 3) repeat 10 times, observe decisions. I can reproduce a refusal about 2/10 on 1.3 but 0/10 on 1.2.

Diego (ML Eng): that matches the customer's delta. Two tracks to triage: model-level safety behavior change (classifier or policy), and runtime/filtering mismatch where policy flags are being evaluated differently (maybe new config cfg_78b).

Sam (Eng Runtime): pulled the logs for req_0a1b2c — safety decision came from the safety microservice at svc-safety-03 returning `refuse` with trace id trace-9f8e. Runtime shows a 502 from safety for some retries earlier in the window. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T22:07:12Z] req=req_0a1b2c -> safety_call start trace=trace-9f8e
[2026-03-10T22:07:12Z] safety svc-safety-03 -> 200 {decision:refuse, version:safety-2026-03-09}
[2026-03-10T22:07:12Z] model redwood-chat-1.3 -> response refused
```

Sam (Eng Runtime): also found HTTP 502 spikes between 22:01-22:10 correlated with canary traffic. Could be cascading retries causing latency and different code paths hitting stricter checks.

Liam (Deploy): cfg_78b included a safety config override for certain enterprise customers to enable 'strict_medical_mode: true' behind a rollout flag. That flag was supposed to be off for non-enterprise customers, but looks like the scope was misconfigured and HealthBot (a mid-market customer) got the flag enabled during canary. I'm digging into the rollout targeting.

Priya (CS): that's likely root cause if true — customer is upset, they flagged it as a negative change in user experience and asked for immediate rollback.

Liam (Deploy): I can roll back the config target for HealthBot and patch the rollout targeting. Rolling back now to remove strict_medical_mode from non-enterprise canary targets. Will post updates.

deploy-bot: rollback cfg_78b targeting for HealthBot initiated by @Liam at 2026-03-10T22:28Z.

Diego (ML Eng): parallel ask: can we ensure safety-classifier versions between 1.2 and 1.3 are compared on the same eval set? If the classifier version changed (safety-2026-03-09) it could shift thresholds. I'll run a quick diff on our eval suite against HealthBot prompt set.

Ava (Support): customer wants concrete repro steps and a mitigation ETA. Suggested messaging: "we pushed a config change in canary that inadvertently enabled a stricter safety mode for some non-enterprise customers; we've removed the flag for you and are monitoring behavior. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem." Customer accepted the temporary rollback but asked for improved testing gating.

Priya (CS): next actions —
- Liam: confirm rollback finished and post confirmation (owner: Liam)
- Sam: check if any runtime caching or KV states could still evaluate old policy for a short TTL (owner: Sam)
- Diego: run classifier/eval diff and report whether model/classifier combo is an independent cause (owner: Diego)
- Ava/Priya: coordinate customer comms and collect 10 failing prompts for regression suite (owner: Priya/Ava)

Liam (Deploy): rollback completed at 2026-03-10T22:33Z. I removed HealthBot from the strict_medical_mode target and pushed a fix to the rollout scoping rules (PR #472).

Sam (Eng Runtime): verified no stuck cache entries. Safety microservice now returning decisions consistent with 1.2 for test prompts. Running a 1k-sample A/B to confirm refusal rate falls back.

Diego (ML Eng): initial eval diff: classifier changes contributed ~2% of the increase but the config flag accounted for ~14% of the jump. Will formalize results and add to the rollout checklist.

Priya (CS): customer update sent: they acknowledged rollback and will monitor for 24h; asked for postmortem and prevention steps.

HealthBot Support (customer): thanks for quick response — we'll keep monitoring. Please let us know when the postmortem is ready.

Ava (Support): recording action items in tracker: CS-8817. ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.

Priya (CS): adding one preventative TODO: add canary-targeting unit tests + safety-aware rollout gating in CI (Diego/Liam).

Diego (ML Eng): agreed, I'll add an automated test comparing refusal rate on a small fixed prompt set before next canary.

Sam (Eng Runtime): closing loop on runtime — I'm not seeing any lingering 5xxs for safety after the rollback window. Will keep monitoring dashboards.

Priya (CS): thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the postmortem and customer notes. :thumbsup:
